speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information with regard to online news site Asia Sentinel, why does the Government require the inclusion of a POFMA correction direction on both the main page of its website and on the page which hosts the article that contains false statements of fact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The Correction Direction will specify the form and manner in which the Correction Notice is to be published.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The intent is to try to have the Correction Notice reach at least as large a readership as the original falsehood, though often this may be difficult to achieve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The inclusion of the POFMA Correction Notice on more than one location on Asia Sentinel’s website is to try and achieve the objective that I stated above.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The Act also allows other orders to be made to get the Correction Notice brought to the attention of the readers who may have read the original falsehoods.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I filed this question because it was a point I raised last month in the course of a speech I made on a Bill and the Minister for Communications and Information invited me to file a Parliamentary Question (PQ) on it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State, at what point is a threshold crossed by which the Government then decides that the Correction Direction not only must be included at the article where the false statement of fact was transmitted, but also the main webpage?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can there not be a question of overreach when you expect the Correction Direction to be on the main webpage as well?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Having it on the article itself would be sufficient because then the reader would know that this particular article is the one that has been flagged out, not every article on the Asia Sentinel website.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think you would characterise this as overreach only if you felt that the inclusion of the Correction Notice, in other words, the correction of the falsity, was, in itself, not necessary or was itself false, or that it was inappropriate to have this viewed by as many people as possible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Singh, who was part of the Select Committee that produced the White Paper that led towards the legislation that turned out to be POFMA, would agree that it is easier for the false statement of fact – a lie travels faster than the truth – and so, you do need to make sure that you have as much coverage as possible when you want to correct the falsity.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The behaviour of people reading online material is not all homogeneous; people access material in different ways.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And it is not often that someone will necessarily go back to the original article after having read it.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, you do need to put the correction in place so that as many readers of the original falsehood as possible will have that corrected.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, we need a variety of tools and, depending on how the site is laid out and how the publisher manages its material, propagates its material, there needs to be some assessment of that done to make sure then that the correction is visible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And even with the tools, such as placing the correction on the main webpage, I am sure the Member would agree, it is unlikely that all the readers of the original falsehood would have that Correction Notice brought to their attention.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I can get the information to Mr Singh.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The reality is that each Correction Notice needs to take into account the design of the feed and the website.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I will get the information to him separately, Sir.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just a follow-up for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because I think the question here is the threshold.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Does the Government treat each site differently or will it treat each site the same?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And in this particular case, I think we need to delve deeper into why that particular Correction Direction required not just the clarification from the POFMA Office to be placed on the article itself, but on the main webpage.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can we expect to see the Government pursuing this approach, given his preamble about how important it is to make sure that lies do not get multiplied much more quickly?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Is the Government changing its approach to be stricter vis-à-vis Correction Directions?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Because the consequence of that Correction Direction is Singaporeans are denied the opportunity to read other articles on Asia Sentinel which contain no false statements of fact.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I think this is a fine line that the POFMA Office needs to consider because I think you have a case when there are false statements of fact, to put out what ought to be the right facts and expect the site to carry them.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But it does sound like overreach when you potentially are almost forcing the site to shut down because you force them to actually put the clarification on the first page, which has nothing to do with the article at hand.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: He said that the action denied Singaporeans the opportunity to read other articles on the Asia Sentinel site.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do not quite understand why the publication of a Correction Notice on its main webpage should in any way impede readers from accessing other articles.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Surely, he would agree that if that Correction Notice is necessary to correct a falsehood, it should be seen by as many readers as possible.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I have no objection with the Correction Direction being on the article itself.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But when you have it on the main webpage, which does not contain the article, but may contain a link to the article, I would grant the Senior Minister of State that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That is why my earlier question was about thresholds.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second question I asked was about the approach of the Government: is this the way it is going to move forward – for Correction Directions for any site, you can expect, not just a Correction Direction on the offending article, but on the main webpage as well?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I am going to assume that he agrees with me that the publication of the Correction Notice on the main webpage does not, in any way, impede a reader from accessing all the other articles on Asia Sentinel's website.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And what that Correction Notice does is add further information and transparency for people to make up their own mind about the facts at hand.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, I hope that is my understanding of his position.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And I hope he will agree that then, there is no overreach or damage done to Asia Sentinel by requiring them to add a notice which essentially carries a correction, in other words, the correct understanding of the facts.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If I take the analogy from what happens in the print publication, I am sure if Mr Singh was concerned about a piece of article in a magazine or a newspaper which he disagreed with, which he required a correction, he would not be satisfied if the only thing that was done was the newspaper went out and published a Correction Notice next to the original article because nobody is going to read the same newspaper again from three or four days ago.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And he would require a notice carried in the same publication in a prominent place that people could read and, especially to do so in a way that as many of the readers of the original false statement will then be better informed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The analogy breaks down a little, clearly; this is an online digital publication and not something in print.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But the intent is the same – to make sure as many of the original readers of that false statement see the Correction Notice, understand the correct facts – and I hope Mr Singh agrees that there is no harm caused by that.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, as I said, I did not quite get an understanding from him that he agreed that we did not, in any way, intend to deny the readers of Asia Sentinel access to the other articles by the publication of the Correction Notice on its main website.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It was a tool to make sure the facts are well-read and well-understood.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think on the first point about whether I agree, I do not agree.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: On the analogy, of course, the analogy break downs, like the Senior Minister of State shared, because you do not expect a print publication to publish an apology on its first page.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, that is the nub of the issue here.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I can accept actually an argument which goes along the line of repeated egregious conduct.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Then, we can analyse and see what the Government's approach is.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But I hope I have clarified every question that the Senior Minister of State asked in his reply to me.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The use of this type of tool, a Correction Notice on the main website, I think, should not be predicated on a certain number of strikes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It needs to take into account, for example, the design of the website, the way in which links are made to other feeds because, otherwise, the process can be gamed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a significant amount of leeway and freedom in how online sites are designed and published.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, we do give an opportunity for the sites to comply, to provide information to the readers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We take into account the fact that the design of the site and the design of the particular article are important and we give an opportunity for people to put things right.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am not sure whether that was an accurate characterisation by the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My understanding was that they followed the Correction Direction, but they only partially followed the Correction Direction.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: There was a clarification on the article itself as required by the POFMA Office but not on the main website.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, you have partial compliance, which means they have not complied with the Correction Direction.
